relationship_records.limitations: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

scientific_assessment.operation: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

functional_dependency.statement: The defined indispensable set must be supplied by diet and supports circulating amino-acid availability. The accepted PM relationship concerns coverage, not increased brain synthesis.

dietary_supply.statement: The canonical milk record explicitly documents a complete essential-amino-acid profile with FAO provenance. A qualitative complete-set edge does not infer quantities from total protein.

scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Identity reconciliation of the already accepted class; no new requirement that each meal provide all nine, no uniform digestibility or neurotransmitter benefit.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing canonical Milk text explicitly supports the complete set. Record that supported qualitative relationship; no food is inferred from total protein and no nine-fold multiplication of admissions or amounts is performed. Other full-profile food edges require separate verified composition.

relationship_records.limitations: Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tyrosine increases brain dopamine or improves a functional or clinical outcome.

upstream_records.limitations: Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

relationship_records.limitations: Dietary B6 provision of PLP precursors is supported, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain GABA synthesis; PLP supports many enzymes and is not GABA-specific.

scientific_assessment.operation: Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.
scientific_assessment.record_origin: Traceability completion of the preserved historical admission; not a new scientific admission or confidence assessment.

functional_dependency.statement: PLP-dependent GAD catalysis is established; dietary deficiency can reduce rat-brain GAD activity through cofactor depletion. The proposition is capacity, not increased synthesis at sufficient intake.

dietary_supply.statement: Human tracer studies establish utilisation of oral B6, including incomplete availability of PN-glucoside. PDXK and human PNPO experiments support vitamer-specific conversion to PLP; this does not measure neuronal cofactor occupancy.

conversion_pathway.process: Vitamer-specific endogenous activation; alternative ordered routes, not one chemical reaction
dependencies: PNPO and FMN for PNP/PMP routes
conversion_pathway.limitations: Alternative routes distinguish PL phosphorylation from PN/PM phosphorylation followed by oxidation. Total food vitamin B6 does not identify vitamer proportions, effective brain exposure or a predictable PLP yield.

evidence.statement: Human PDXK and PNPO enzymology supports distinct substrate-specific activation routes to the same canonical PLP target.

dependencies: ATP–divalent-metal substrate complex; metal effects depend on assay context
steps.limitations: PN and PM phosphorylation produces PNP and PMP, not PLP directly. In-vitro metal efficacy does not establish a dietary zinc requirement.

evidence.statement: Human PDXK phosphorylates PL, PN and PM to their respective 5-prime phosphates.

dependencies: ATP–divalent-metal substrate complex; metal effects depend on assay context
steps.limitations: PN and PM phosphorylation produces PNP and PMP, not PLP directly. In-vitro metal efficacy does not establish a dietary zinc requirement.

evidence.statement: Human PDXK phosphorylates PL, PN and PM to their respective 5-prime phosphates.

steps.limitations: Applies to phosphorylated PN/PM; PL does not require this oxidation step. Enzymology does not quantify neuronal PLP occupancy or food-level conversion yield.

evidence.statement: Human PNPO oxidises PNP and PMP to PLP with enzyme-bound FMN.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing structured composition and provisional food research for this exact canonical input were inspected. Reuse these source/form-qualified foods; do not infer an effective food dose or invent additional relationships.

functional_dependency.statement: Riboflavin supplies FMN and FAD used by methionine-synthase reductase to regenerate active B12-dependent methionine synthase.

dietary_supply.statement: The same canonical nutrient is supplied by the inspected food records. Tissue uptake and homeostasis remain distinct from an effect of extra intake.

conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin kinase (RFK) phosphorylates riboflavin to FMN using ATP.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Enzyme identity does not quantify tissue cofactor supply or flux after a meal.

evidence.statement: Human RFK catalyses riboflavin phosphorylation; UniProt Q969G6 entry 195 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 14357.

conversion_pathway.process: FLAD1 FAD synthase adenylates FMN with ATP to form FAD.
conversion_pathway.limitations: FAD production and enzyme loading depend on cellular context; no fixed food-to-FAD yield is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human FLAD1 catalyses FMN adenylation; UniProt Q8NFF5 entry 182 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 17237.

relationship_records.limitations: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

relationship_records.limitations: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.

upstream_records.limitations: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

relationship_records.limitations: Human MAT structural and enzymological evidence establishes catalytic capacity. Ordinary food supply is distinct from measured MAT flux; no benefit from additional magnesium in replete people or universal methylation increase is asserted.

scientific_assessment.operation: Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.

functional_dependency.statement: Magnesium supplies the catalytic ion coordinating ATP-derived phosphate groups in human MAT-dependent SAM formation.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

scientific_assessment.operation: Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.

functional_dependency.statement: Potassium supplies the active-site catalytic ion supporting phosphoryl-group positioning in human MAT-dependent SAM formation.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

relationship_records.limitations: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.

upstream_records.limitations: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

relationship_records.limitations: Only the choline-to-betaine methyl-supply route is admitted here, not choline membrane or neurotransmitter roles. Oxidation, predominantly hepatic/renal BHMT activity and alternative supply constrain interpretation. Increased integrated cycle flux or improved branch balance or benefit from additional choline in replete individuals is not established.

upstream_records.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

food_sources.material: UK mature broccoli, sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, with and without 1 g brown mustard powder

presence_records.evidence: Okunade, Niranjan, Ghawi, Kuhnle and Methven (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980. Formation identity also rests on Fahey et al. (1997).
presence_records.limitations: Sulforaphane forms from glucoraphanin when myrosinase is active. In one cooked-broccoli study the amount depended on preparation, and it is not entered as a per-100 g nutrient.

presence_records.label: Sulforaphane
presence_records.public_note: One UK broccoli lot, cooked sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, formed 1.06 µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight. Adding 1 g brown mustard powder raised that to 8.58 µmol/g dry weight. Twelve adults who ate 200 g excreted 9.8 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours, and 44.7 µmol/g creatinine with the mustard. These figures are not a sulforaphane amount for every 100 g of broccoli.
presence_records.source_note: Okunade et al. (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980, Table 1 and the 24-hour urine result. Table 1, µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight: raw 2.05 ± 0.25; sous vide 100 °C for 20 minutes 1.06 ± 0.18; the same cooked broccoli plus 1 g brown mustard powder 8.58 ± 0.33. 8.58 / 1.06 = 8.1, which the paper reports as an 8-fold increase. One results sentence prints the mustard result as 8.58 ± 0.13; the table figure is used here. Urine, 12 adults, 200 g of that cooked broccoli: 9.8 ± 5.1 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours without mustard, and 44.7 ± 33.9 with 1 g mustard. 44.7 / 9.8 = 4.6 from the published means. The paper's average of each person's increase is 4.7-fold, with individual increases from 1.7-fold to 10-fold. Sous-vide myrosinase loss in the same paper: 40% after 2 minutes, 90% after 6 minutes, and no measurable activity after 8 minutes. The study did not report a glucoraphanin concentration, and the dry-weight results are not converted to a fresh 100 g amount. Fahey et al. (1997) identifies sulforaphane as the myrosinase product of glucoraphanin; it is not the source of these figures.

calculation.not_a_panel_amount: Dry-weight and creatinine-normalised study results. No moisture figure is given, so they are not scaled to per 100 g fresh broccoli.

relationship_records.limitations: Curated human SOD1 and experimental structural evidence support a structural capacity relationship, not zinc-dependent catalysis identical to copper. Human dietary SOD responses vary by isoform and status; extra zinc can disturb copper availability. No general oxidative-stress improvement or benefit above adequacy is established.

scientific_assessment.operation: Balance reactive oxygen species production and clearance so net oxidative pressure stays within tolerable limits.

functional_dependency.statement: Zinc supplies the structural metal stabilising human SOD1, supporting native Cu/Zn-SOD capacity; copper is the redox-active catalytic metal.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

mechanism_engagement.statement: Defined oral DHA exposure attenuated selected post-exercise LPS-stimulated mononuclear-cell cytokine-production responses in the tested human context.

dietary_exposure.statement: The human experiment administered an oral DHA-enriched food matrix and confirmed erythrocyte DHA incorporation. Existing fish-composition records provide the same fatty acid but do not reproduce that beverage dose or prove cytokine effects of ordinary foods.

scientific_assessment.operation: Sustain efficient electron transport so mitochondria generate ATP without excessive electron leakage.

functional_dependency.statement: Copper supplies the CuA/CuB centres required for complex-IV electron transfer and oxygen reduction. Dietary copper deficiency impairs cardiac cytochrome-c-oxidase capacity in rats.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

relationship_records.limitations: The review identifies the salvage substrate. It does not show that eating more nicotinamide, once intake is adequate, raises NAD⁺. The myopathy niacin study used nicotinic acid at pharmacological doses.

Supplemental NR chloride at 100–1000 mg is not an effective milk dose. Blood responses do not establish neuronal or mitochondrial NAD delivery, redox flux, superiority to adequate niacin or clinical benefit. Intestinal metabolism and tissue salvage can differ from the displayed intracellular NRK route; other NAD precursors remain alternatives.

scientific_assessment.operation: Maintain NAD⁺ availability so redox reactions and mitochondrial signalling stay adequately powered.
scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Supplemental NR chloride at 100–1000 mg is not an effective milk dose. Blood responses do not establish neuronal or mitochondrial NAD delivery, redox flux, superiority to adequate niacin or clinical benefit. Intestinal metabolism and tissue salvage can differ from the displayed intracellular NRK route; other NAD precursors remain alternatives.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Primary milk analysis and the canonical Milk record were inspected. A qualitative cow-milk NR relationship is recorded with source/material limits; no concentration is transplanted into the USDA whole-milk nutrition table. No NR edge is inferred for plant milks, cheese or other dairy without evidence.

functional_dependency.statement: Dietary nicotinamide riboside can supply the NAD precursor pool through supported salvage reactions, sustaining NAD-availability capacity.

dietary_supply.statement: Primary chemical analysis identifies NR in raw and commercial cow milk. This establishes dietary occurrence, separately from oral supplement-induced blood NAD responses.

conversion_pathway.process: Human NRK1 phosphorylates beta-NR to beta-NMN using ATP.
conversion_pathway.limitations: An established intracellular route is not proof that all oral NR reaches each tissue intact; parallel degradation/salvage can contribute.

evidence.statement: NRK1 curated reaction, entry version 170, Rhea 14017, retrieved 26 October 2026.

conversion_pathway.process: NMN adenylyltransferase adenylates oxidised beta-NMN with ATP to form oxidised NAD.
conversion_pathway.limitations: NMNAT1 establishes reaction identity; other isoforms/transport determine compartmental provision. No fixed dietary conversion yield or mitochondrial/brain endpoint is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human NMNAT1, entry version 202, Rhea 21360, retrieved 26 October 2026.

reasons: Presence-only: no quantitative observation

relationship_records.limitations: In five adults with mitochondrial myopathy, niacin at 750–1,000 mg/day raised blood NAD⁺ and brought muscle NAD⁺ to the control level. That is medical dosing in a deficiency disease, not a result for adequate everyday intake, and attention was not measured.
Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

relationship_records.limitations: Admission concerns a circulating hormone response in studied supplement/enriched-oil contexts. It does not establish adipose secretion, receptor sensitivity, universal benefit, ordinary-food efficacy or a food-effective dose. Mixture and carrier effects are not attributed to DHA alone; DHA-specific attribution uses the separate DHA-versus-EPA trial.

scientific_assessment.operation: Regulate adipose-derived endocrine signalling and local glucocorticoid responsiveness to communicate metabolic state and coordinate hormonal adaptation.

mechanism_engagement.statement: Defined oral DHA changed the circulating adiponectin signal in selected human contexts. This endocrine-response proposition does not claim local secretion, synthesis or receptor engagement.

dietary_exposure.statement: Oral DHA was administered in a defined re-esterified-triglyceride supplement; enriched-oil and mixed fish-oil exposures are assessed separately. Existing food composition establishes dietary presence, not trial equivalence.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing food composition records and structured DHA edges cover multiple animal foods and algal oil; source, material, preparation and presence records were examined separately. Unmapped existing composition observations stay provisional. No new food or food-effective quantity is invented; trial formulations are not treated as equivalent to ordinary foods.

scientific_assessment.scope: Circulating adipose-derived endocrine signal modulation, not local production or physiological/clinical improvement.
